A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EBD research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J support a reliable comparison despite renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, CorInfoMax-EBD results, gradient-alignment analyses, correlation trajectories, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds CIFAR-100 evaluation and a CNN activation–error correlation experiment.

M1.justification: The EBD objectives, truncated updates, regularizers, forward broadcasting, and CorInfoMax integration are retained. Newly displayed batch-size-one formulas specialize existing equations; the CIFAR-100 CNN applies the existing method.

E1.justification: v3 adds CIFAR-100's 100-class image classification task to the retained MNIST and CIFAR-10 coverage (Section 4, Table 2). This broadens coverage within the existing image-classification domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including BP, DFA, DFA+E, NN-GEVB, MS-GEVB, and CorInfoMax-EP in their respective comparisons. CIFAR-100 reuses BP and DFA; newly cited related methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The new CIFAR-100 protocol introduces a different CNN, dropout, training augmentation, and six-view test averaging. EBD/DFA use 300 epochs, while BP uses cross-entropy and 200 epochs (Appendix I, Tables 15 and 19). Appendix J adds a 30-epoch CNN diagnostic using SGD; retained experimental settings otherwise match.

E4.justification: Appendix J.1 adds a test of whether activation–error correlation decay during backpropagation extends from MLPs to a five-layer CNN on CIFAR-10 (Figure 11). Existing gradient-alignment, truncation, and MLP loss-criterion analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five-run averaging and report standard-deviation envelopes for learning curves. The CIFAR-100 results follow the existing reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds CIFAR-100 accuracies of 45.9±0.69 for EBD, 41.9±0.32 for DFA, and 60.5±0.17 for BP with cross-entropy (Table 2), plus CNN correlation-decay results. Section 4 also newly reports comparable BP accuracy with MSE and cross-entropy on MNIST/CIFAR-10. Matched earlier accuracy and runtime values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The MMSE lemmas, orthogonality theorems, assumptions, proofs, update derivations, and complexity analysis are retained. The added single-sample equations and revised notation do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of MMSE-grounded error broadcasting, three-factor learning, competitive benchmark performance, and demonstrated 10-layer CorInfoMax-EBD training. Additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly explains why BP's neuron-specific backward signal differs from the neuroscientific interpretation of a three-factor rule. Appendix J extends the interpretation of correlation decay to CNNs. Existing scalability, computational-cost, and biological-plausibility limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a URL for the paper's own implementation and documents CIFAR-100 architecture, augmentation, dropout, and hyperparameters, plus the CNN diagnostic settings. It also explicitly identifies pooling stride and the main BP table's MSE criterion. These disclosures supplement the extensive implementation information already in v2.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds the HSIC bottleneck and work by Akrout, Frenkel, and Xiao concerning weight transport, feedback-free learning, and scalability. These four additions modestly broaden research positioning; the established comparisons with DFA and other approaches remain.

P1.justification: v3 streamlines introductory paragraphs, expands the three-factor explanation, clarifies notation and batch indexing, and moves learning curves to Appendix I.10. These are localized revisions within the retained overall narrative and section structure.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes displays: it adds a three-factor diagram and new experimental figures/tables, merges separate dataset hyperparameter tables, and relocates learning curves. The original CorInfoMax accuracy panels move to Figure 8. Figure 6(g–h) instead duplicates its CNN panels while retaining CorInfoMax captions, introducing a presentation error.

improvement.justification: The CIFAR-100 benchmark and CNN correlation diagnostic modestly strengthen empirical support, while clearer exposition and implementation access information improve usability. These gains outweigh the localized Figure 6 labeling error because the correct CorInfoMax curves remain in Figure 8. Different BP/EBD budgets and dropout settings limit the new benchmark comparison; the core method and theory remain unchanged.
